what: Republic Services collects rubbish and recycling across the United States and Canada, and owns the landfills, transfer stations and recycling centres it sends the material to, plus a growing hazardous waste business.
customers: Municipalities under long-term contracts, plus commercial, industrial and construction customers.
money: landfill and transfer station fees, including from third-party haulers
recycled commodities, hazardous waste and renewable energy from landfill gas
moat: Landfill permits that are almost impossible to obtain, which forces competing haulers to pay it for disposal.
risks: Volume growth depends on construction and industrial activity
Debt of about $14 billion is typical for the sector but limits flexibility
Recycled commodity prices swing and affect that segment
Labour and fuel costs can outpace contracted price increases
opportunities: Contracts include inflation-linked price increases, which protects margins
Polymer recycling centres and renewable natural gas projects add higher-margin revenue
Acquiring small local haulers steadily adds route density
watch: Core pricing against volume and the ramp-up of its polymer and renewable gas facilities.
